all_findings.description:
In `detect_finding_id_collisions`, the model‑id collection line
model_ids = sorted({
    getattr(f, "model_id", "?")
    for f in findings
    if getattr(f, "finding_id", None) == fid
})
uses a bare string `"?"` as the default when `model_id` is missing. The `cross_model` flag is later computed as `len(model_ids) > 1`. If any finding in a collision set lacks `model_id`, the set will contain `"?"` alongside real model IDs, causing `cross_model` to be `True` even when all the colliding findings come from the *same* model (some of which happen to be missing the attribute). This misclassifies a same‑model duplicate as a cross‑model collision, directly corrupting the evidence the UUID‑namespace gate is supposed to decide on.

The function signature `def detect_finding_id_collisions(findings: List[Any], round_idx: int = -1) -> ...` provides a default value of `-1` for the round index. If a caller omits the round index (by accident or incomplete integration), every collision record produced in that call will have `"round": -1`. This can silently pollute the evidence accumulator, making it impossible to distinguish missing data from a genuine round index of `-1`, and may skew post‑mortem statistics (e.g., collision rate per round). The docstring does not warn that the default is a sentinel, nor does it raise if a proper round index is missing.

In `detect_finding_id_collisions`, the set comprehension that collects
`model_ids` uses `getattr(f, "model_id", "?")` at line 97 (current file).
When a `Finding` object omits the `model_id` attribute (or has it set to a
falsy value), every such object contributes the identical string `"?"` to the
set.  As a result:
• two findings from different models that both lack `model_id` will produce
  `model_ids = ["?"]`, `cross_model = False` — a false negative.
• two findings from the same model that both lack `model_id` will also show
  `cross_model = False`, which is correct but by accident.

The `"?"` sentinel destroys the information the detector is meant to capture:
it cannot distinguish “three distinct models, none with a model_id” from “one
model that emitted the same id three times”.  Evidence: running the function
with three `Finding`-like objects whose `finding_id` is "F001" and none of
which have a `model_id` attribute produces a record
`{"round":0, "finding_id":"F001", "count":3, "model_ids":["?"], "cross_model":False}`,
which is misleading.

all_findings.description:
In `detect_finding_id_collisions`, line 88–96:
model_ids = sorted({
    getattr(f, "model_id", "?")
    for f in findings
    if getattr(f, "finding_id", None) == fid
})
rec = {
    ...
    "model_ids": model_ids,
    "cross_model": len(model_ids) > 1,
}
The use of `"?"` as a default for missing `model_id` collapses all unknown model identities into a single sentinel. This makes the `cross_model` flag unreliable:

* False negative (missed cross‑model collision): Two findings from *different* models that both lack `model_id` → both become `"?"` → set has one element → `cross_model` = `False`.
* False positive (wrongly flagged cross‑model): One finding from model *A* with `model_id="A"` and one from *A* with `model_id=None` → set contains `{"A", "?"}` → `cross_model` = `True`.
